In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of drugs on the rates of synthesis of proteins of the liver organelles of experimental animals.

the effect of a single oral dose of the drugs phenobarbital (PB) (50 mg/kg), 3-methyl cholanthrene (MC) (20 mg/kg), PCB (50 mg/kg) and cycloheximides (CHI) (10 mg/kg) on the in vivo rate of synthesis of the following proteins: microsomal and mitochondrial bound cytochromes, reductases and serum albumin.
the effect of drugs, administered individually, on the rates of synthesis of the proteins of liver microsomal and mitochondrial membranes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all the treatments tested were found to affect the rates of synthesis of the liver organelle proteins.
the effect of the drugs on the in vitro rates of synthesis of liver organelle proteins is dependent on the drug, the protein, the organelle and the dose.
the effect of the drugs on the in vitro rates of synthesis of the proteins was not always the same as their effect on the in vivo synthesis rates of the same proteins.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

1) the rate of synthesis for all the above proteins was increased following treatment with the inducers; 2) the rate of protein synthesis was decreased following treatments with the inhibitors; and 3) in all cases the rates of protein synthesis for the proteins in each of the above organelles were increased or decreased in the same manner as that of the cytochrome b and reductase proteins.

the effects of drugs on the rate of protein synthesis are dependent on their effects on the rate of mRNA synthesis, on the rate of translation and on the stability of the proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of synthesis in the liver of these proteins is highly sensitive to the presence of drugs.
the effects of the drugs were specific for the organelles from which the proteins were isolated.
